Subject: RE: Fwd: MSA indemnity redlines (Neptune)

Naomi — thanks, looped in legal commentary below.

Summary recommendation (short): we can offer Option A (Defend & Control) as the primary position with the following guardrails:
- Scope: Redwood will defend and indemnify Neptune for third-party claims that the Redwood service, as delivered, infringes a third party’s IP. Exclude claims arising from: (i) customer-provided models or data; (ii) modifications made by Neptune or third parties; (iii) OSS components expressly carved out.
- Defense control: Redwood will assume defense using counsel of Redwood’s choosing; Redwood will not settle any claim that imposes an obligation on Neptune or admits fault on Neptune without Neptune’s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld).
- Notice & cooperation: Neptune must provide prompt written notice and reasonable cooperation; our proposed evidence list is intentionally narrow (see attached snippet) — notice + basic logs + reproduction steps.
- Cap: propose a per-order-form cap of $2,000,000 for IP indemnity (higher than their $1M ask but reduces residual risk). We can tier caps by customer spend if needed.
- Insurance: require vendor to maintain commercial general liability and tech E&O with minimum $1M per occurrence; if insurance is in force at the time of the claim, escrow will not be required.

Redline snippet (suggested language for the MSA):
"Vendor shall defend, at its expense, any claim brought by a third party alleging that the Vendor Service as provided infringes such third party’s patent, copyright or trade secret. Vendor's indemnification obligation shall not apply to claims arising out of (a) Customer-provided models or data; (b) Customer modifications; or (c) open-source software explicitly identified in Schedule X."

Operational asks for Ben (technical): 1) confirm we can retain request logs + model input hashes + KV-cache metadata for 90 days in US-hosted accounts; 2) estimate cost to extend retention to 12 months if Neptune asks.

Rationale: Defend & control limits litigation cost exposure (we control defense strategy) while the cap limits aggregate liability. Insurance-first removes the operational burden of placing funds in escrow.

If this direction looks good I can draft the redline and a ~1 paragraph talking points doc for the call with Neptune counsel.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
